attributes.label: Acidity potential
assumptions: TA is an acid-load proxy, not measured sourness. pH, acid identity, buffers and masking affect perception.
M2 source-water alkalinity is already included in TA; hardness is not given a universal flavour benefit.
CGA and unresolved buffers can contribute to TA without the same sensory effect as individual organic acids.

attributes.label: Bitterness potential
assumptions: Family labels describe compounds, not a prediction of the perceived bitterness type.
Lumped lactones and phenylindanes have different molecular potencies; reference scales are not water detection thresholds.
Caffeine weight is an arbitrary relative scaling, not its percentage of perceived bitterness. Melanoidin suppression and other mixture effects are unresolved.
DKPs, mozambioside products and other bitter compounds are omitted because contribution and mixture potency are insufficiently constrained.

attributes.label: Astringency correlate
assumptions: This is an empirical-direction correlate, not a salivary-protein or friction model. CGAs need not be the molecules causing astringency.
Sip sequence, saliva, suspended particles, brew nonuniformity and individual oral responses are not predicted.

attributes.label: Body / texture potential
assumptions: TDS uses true coffee solubles, excluding source minerals and refractometer temperature bias.
Polymers already occur within TDS; this is an explicit composition reweighting, not a sum of distinct masses or measured viscosity.
Lipid transfer is an M2 phase-recovery prior. Droplet size, suspended fines, foam stability and temperature-dependent viscosity are unresolved.
All taste coefficients are grade D estimates. No espresso sensory panel was used to fit or validate these indices.
Input uncertainty bands propagate selected scenarios only; missing sensory mechanisms and individual differences remain outside those bands.
Chemistry uses its stated reference temperature. Serving temperature is recorded without a perceptual correction; no hot-cup taste prediction is made.
Sweetness, aroma notes, balance, liking and a quality score are not inferred from extractable sugars, OAVs, TDS or EY.
Acidity, bitterness, astringency and body are separate dimensions; index values must not be compared across dimensions or summed.

notes: Scenario percentiles are conditional on selected illustrative input supports; they are not calibrated confidence intervals or a probability of the real shot falling inside the band.

Every ensemble member and the baseline preview use Tier 0; the central shot retains its requested tier. Tier 0 approximation error and model discrepancy are not included in these bands, and the Tier 1 central value may lie outside them.

PSD bins share a diameter scale; fines bins share one reweighting factor. Compound composition inventories share one multiplier. M2 source-water alkalinity is already included in TA; hardness is not given a universal flavour benefit.
CGA and unresolved buffers can contribute to TA without the same sensory effect as individual organic acids.

attributes.label: Bitterness potential
assumptions: Family labels describe compounds, not a prediction of the perceived bitterness type.
Lumped lactones and phenylindanes have different molecular potencies; reference scales are not water detection thresholds.
Caffeine weight is an arbitrary relative scaling, not its percentage of perceived bitterness. Melanoidin suppression and other mixture effects are unresolved.
DKPs, mozambioside products and other bitter compounds are omitted because contribution and mixture potency are insufficiently constrained.

attributes.label: Astringency correlate
assumptions: This is an empirical-direction correlate, not a salivary-protein or friction model. CGAs need not be the molecules causing astringency.
Sip sequence, saliva, suspended particles, brew nonuniformity and individual oral responses are not predicted.

attributes.label: Body / texture potential
assumptions: TDS uses true coffee solubles, excluding source minerals and refractometer temperature bias.
Polymers already occur within TDS; this is an explicit composition reweighting, not a sum of distinct masses or measured viscosity.
Lipid transfer is an M2 phase-recovery prior. Droplet size, suspended fines, foam stability and temperature-dependent viscosity are unresolved.
All taste coefficients are grade D estimates. No espresso sensory panel was used to fit or validate these indices.
Input uncertainty bands propagate selected scenarios only; missing sensory mechanisms and individual differences remain outside those bands.
Chemistry uses its stated reference temperature. Serving temperature is recorded without a perceptual correction; no hot-cup taste prediction is made.
Sweetness, aroma notes, balance, liking and a quality score are not inferred from extractable sugars, OAVs, TDS or EY.
Acidity, bitterness, astringency and body are separate dimensions; index values must not be compared across dimensions or summed.

notes: Scenario percentiles are conditional on selected illustrative input supports; they are not calibrated confidence intervals or a probability of the real shot falling inside the band.

Every ensemble member and the baseline preview use Tier 0; the central shot retains its requested tier. Tier 0 approximation error and model discrepancy are not included in these bands, and the Tier 1 central value may lie outside them.

PSD bins share a diameter scale; fines bins share one reweighting factor. Compound composition inventories share one multiplier. Water minerals, hardness, alkalinity and TDS share a multiplier, preserving baseline ratios; source pH varies independently. These correlations are assumptions, not measurements.

Measured means narrower illustrative measurement supports, not zero uncertainty. Fixed groups and explicit source parameter overrides stay fixed. Selecting unknown can vary an explicitly entered recipe input.
Trajectory bands align fractional recorded duration including post-stop drip, not physical time. Spatial fields are not pooled because particle radii and bed geometry can change.

notes: Scenario percentiles are conditional on selected illustrative input supports; they are not calibrated confidence intervals or a probability of the real shot falling inside the band.

Every ensemble member and the baseline preview use Tier 0; the central shot retains its requested tier. Tier 0 approximation error and model discrepancy are not included in these bands, and the Tier 1 central value may lie outside them.

PSD bins share a diameter scale; fines bins share one reweighting factor. Compound composition inventories share one multiplier. Water minerals, hardness, alkalinity and TDS share a multiplier, preserving baseline ratios; source pH varies independently. These correlations are assumptions, not measurements.

Measured means narrower illustrative measurement supports, not zero uncertainty. Fixed groups and explicit source parameter overrides stay fixed. Selecting unknown can vary an explicitly entered recipe input.
Trajectory bands align fractional recorded duration including post-stop drip, not physical time. Spatial fields are not pooled because particle radii and bed geometry can change.

unsupported.model_discrepancy: No calibrated physics discrepancy, taste coefficient, sensory threshold or Tier 0/Tier 1 discrepancy distribution is available.
unsupported.spatial: No spatial bands: class radii, geometry and snapshot grids differ between members; view the central simulation spatial result.

assumptions: TA is an acid-load proxy, not measured sourness. pH, acid identity, buffers and masking affect perception.
M2 source-water alkalinity is already included in TA; hardness is not given a universal flavour benefit.
CGA and unresolved buffers can contribute to TA without the same sensory effect as individual organic acids.

attributes.label: Bitterness potential
assumptions: Family labels describe compounds, not a prediction of the perceived bitterness type.
Lumped lactones and phenylindanes have different molecular potencies; reference scales are not water detection thresholds.
Caffeine weight is an arbitrary relative scaling, not its percentage of perceived bitterness. Melanoidin suppression and other mixture effects are unresolved.
DKPs, mozambioside products and other bitter compounds are omitted because contribution and mixture potency are insufficiently constrained.

attributes.label: Astringency correlate
assumptions: This is an empirical-direction correlate, not a salivary-protein or friction model. CGAs need not be the molecules causing astringency.
Sip sequence, saliva, suspended particles, brew nonuniformity and individual oral responses are not predicted.

attributes.label: Body / texture potential
assumptions: TDS uses true coffee solubles, excluding source minerals and refractometer temperature bias.
Polymers already occur within TDS; this is an explicit composition reweighting, not a sum of distinct masses or measured viscosity.
Lipid transfer is an M2 phase-recovery prior. Droplet size, suspended fines, foam stability and temperature-dependent viscosity are unresolved.
All taste coefficients are grade D estimates. No espresso sensory panel was used to fit or validate these indices.
Input uncertainty bands propagate selected scenarios only; missing sensory mechanisms and individual differences remain outside those bands.
Chemistry uses its stated reference temperature. Serving temperature is recorded without a perceptual correction; no hot-cup taste prediction is made.
Sweetness, aroma notes, balance, liking and a quality score are not inferred from extractable sugars, OAVs, TDS or EY.
Acidity, bitterness, astringency and body are separate dimensions; index values must not be compared across dimensions or summed.

registry.interpretation: Estimated scenario supports and heuristic taste coefficients; provenance is not calibration.

limitations: Checks are software verification and mechanistic direction checks, not independent sensory validation.
The scenario distributions and widths are estimated modelling judgements; empirical coverage is unmeasured.
Scenario quantiles omit structural model error, kinetic uncertainty and taste-mapping error.
Taste indices are relative explanatory indices, not panel scores, liking or coffee quality.
Dilution checks hold the extracted cup inventory fixed and add water; they do not predict a longer extraction.
Tier 0 versus Tier 1 discrepancy is reported separately and is not absorbed by enlarging scenario bands.
M1 fit values are preserved, but their prior scientific limitations and the blocked M2 V7 gate remain.
Timing is a local wall-clock observation including Python boundary overhead, not a browser performance guarantee.
